title: DTAB Panel Recommends Continuing Doorstep Medicine Delivery Amid E-Pharmacy Concerns

contentHtml:
New Delhi: The Centre is likely to continue allowing pharmacies to deliver certain medicines directly to patients' homes through both offline and online channels. A sub-committee constituted under India's apex drug advisory panel has recommended retaining the provision, noting that withdrawing it could create difficulties for people living in rural and remote areas, elderly patients and those suffering from chronic illnesses.

The recommendation comes amid concerns over the continued use of the provision by e-pharmacies and digital medicine-delivery platforms. The issue was recently considered by the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB) during its meeting on 27 August.

The doorstep delivery facility was introduced through a notification issued on 26 March 2020, during the Covid-19 pandemic. The measure was intended to help patients, particularly elderly individuals and those with chronic conditions, who faced difficulties visiting pharmacies regularly during the pandemic.

Under the provision, retail pharmacies were permitted to deliver certain medicines within the same revenue district. The rules also covered some Schedule H medicines, subject to conditions such as a valid prescription and proper maintenance of transaction records.

Pharmacies and chemists have, however, sought the withdrawal of the notification, arguing that it was introduced as a pandemic-related measure and is now being misused by online platforms.

According to a recent media report in Live Mint, doctors have supported continuing doorstep medicine delivery, particularly for elderly and chronic-care patients. However, they have stressed the need for stronger safeguards covering prescription compliance, proper storage and handling of medicines, authorized dispensing channels and accountability in online deliveries.
